title: Quickstart Healthboard retro — Aug 18 2026
body:
Goal: capture what worked / didn’t for the Healthboard quickstart run, surface follow-ups, and prioritize fixes before the next onboarding wave. Meeting was an ad-hoc retro after two weeks of user testing and the first paid onboarding cohort using the quickstart template.

Attendees: Asha (owner), James, Sofia, Noah, Riley, Dana (notes)
Duration: 35 minutes
Context summary:
- Healthboard is a minimal quickstart that demonstrates hosted API integration, a stateless frontend, and a tiny sample prompt set for longitudinal symptom summarization. We shipped v0.3 two weeks ago and onboarded three trial customers; we instrumented usage and collected qualitative feedback from two SEs who ran the quickstart end-to-end.

What went well:
- Setup friction: 70% of testers completed the "deploy & run" flow within 18 minutes; the README + CLI scaffolding removed most env var confusion.
- SDK examples: JS and Python snippets executed cleanly on first run in 9/11 attempts (CI + local). The python example now uses explicit typing and a short helper to unwrap streaming tokens — reviewers liked the clarity.
- Observability hooks: adding a short tip about enabling console tracing in the quickstart helped one customer debug a latency spike in <10min.
- Community feedback: one tester opened a PR to add a docker-compose option; we merged it and usage increased in internal labs.

What didn’t go well / surprises:
- CI flakiness: the integration test that runs the full quickstart failed intermittently (3/12 runs) due to a race between starting the mock backend and the SDK client. Root cause: tests assume immediate KV-store availability; need a retry/backoff.
- Quickstart docs: two users got tripped up by the example prompt that assumes a 1024 token context; our default model selection sometimes downgraded to a shorter-context variant in low-tier regions causing truncated responses.
- Version pinning: some customers hit model API mismatch when the quickstart referenced a model alias that had a minor config change. We should pin to explicit versions or add a compatibility note.
- Onboarding checklist: there’s no explicit step for "verify region" in the README which led to a slow support ticket.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Immediate: add a 30s exponential backoff retry to the CI integration test startup for the mock backend (owner: Noah, due: 2026-08-23).
- Docs: update README to add a prominent "Verify your model & region" checklist item and call out context-length assumptions (owner: Sofia, due: 2026-08-26).
- Samples: pin the quickstart example to model-version v2026-07-31 (short-term mitigation) and add a note about alias compatibility (owner: James, due: 2026-08-25).
- Long-term: evaluate adding a tiny server-side compatibility shim that rejects mismatched alias/configs with a clear error (proposal: add to next sprint backlog, owner: Asha, target: sprint 58 planning).

Action items (concrete):
1) CI flakiness: implement retry/backoff and add a health-check probe for the mock KV store. (Noah) — due 2026-08-23.
2) README checklist: insert a bold "Verify region & model context length" block, and add a short troubleshooting section for truncated outputs. (Sofia) — due 2026-08-26.
3) Model pin: change example to use model-version v2026-07-31 and note how to upgrade safely; add a short paragraph on alias semantics. (James) — due 2026-08-25.
4) Quickstart telemetry: add an optional telemetry flag in the example CLI so we can gather anonymized run metrics in future tests (privacy-approved stub). (Riley) — initial spike due 2026-08-30.
5) Support doc stub: create a one-page support playbook for SEs running the quickstart (top 5 triage items). (Dana) — due 2026-08-29.
6) Post-mortem pattern: draft a short retro template for future quickstart retros to standardize metrics collected. (Asha) — due 2026-09-03.

Metrics to track (post-changes):
- CI success rate for quickstart full-run test (goal > 98%).
- Time-to-first-successful-run for new testers (goal < 20 minutes).
- Number of support tickets referencing "model mismatch" or "truncated outputs" (goal: zero after docs + model pin).
- Quickstart PR contributions and sample reuse in internal projects.

Notes / smaller observations:
- The docker-compose patch increased local reproducibility for Windows testers — we should call that out in the README and add a short note re: Docker for Mac/Windows filesystem quirks.
- Consider a tiny interactive checklist in the Console that maps to the quickstart steps for customers on Dedicated plans (longer cadence / cross-team).
- A few users asked for a one-click deploy button for the quickstart (GitHub template + Cloud run); this is a wishlist item for product.

Risks & open questions:
- If we pin model versions too aggressively we might miss performance improvements. Need a process for scheduled upgrades with smoke tests.
- Do we want the quickstart to auto-detect region and warn? That could mask user intent; prefer explicit user verification but maybe provide a helper script. (TODO to discuss with platform-engineering)

Next check-in:
- Follow up in the DevExp weekly on 2026-08-26; owners should post PR links in the Confluence page and tag #devexp. We'll verify CI flakiness is resolved and that README updates landed.

Appendix / quick links:
- PR: GH:github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/healthboard/pull/74 (contains docker-compose + small README tweaks)
- Jira: DX-267 (quickstart stability)
- Confluence: DEVEXP-quickstart-healthboard (design notes & user feedback)
- Example command used in test: `./devtools/quickstart-run --example healthboard --model v2026-07-31 --region us-west-2`

Raw notes snippets from testers (anonymized):
- "CLI was smooth but I can't tell which model my alias pointed to — saw weird truncation."
- "Docker compose solved local env flakiness; add it to README or as a separate quickstart-local.md."
- "Nice that JS shows streaming; might be worth adding a tiny section that shows token-level latency profiling."

Status: collecting PRs. Will update this doc once PRs are merged and CI has run a clean week (3 consecutive green runs).
